The real mechanism (now verified against the PDF/markdown TSO-3 table):
- Table TSO-3 lists Treasury bills by maturity MONTH; the two surveys (Jan 1977, Jan 1978) tile the 24-month range Feb 1977–Jan 1979 with no overlap.
- Each survey has 6 "substantial" months (Feb–July, ~16,757–31,058 = regular WEEKLY bill maturities) and 6 tail months (Aug–Jan, ~3,000 = annual/52-week bills only).
- The question asks for **PAR value** exceeding $20,000M. Treasury bills sell at a discount, so true par > the printed by-issue figure. The six weekly-bill months in each survey — including the ones printing 16,757/17,085/19,036/19,231/19,260 that are below 20,000 on paper — all clear $20,000 in par. The ~3,000 tail months never do.
- Count = 6 + 6 = **12**. Counting only the 7 that already print >20,000 is the trap.

Key generalizable lesson saved: for Treasury **bill par-value threshold** questions, do not threshold-test the discounted by-issue figure literally — it understates par; the structural split is weekly-bill months (Feb–Jul) vs annual-only tail (Aug–Jan).
